expectation: Membrane staining on macrophages and dendritic cells, and in some tumours on tumour-cell nests as rings around the cells. Amount differs from tumour to tumour, so some cores are positive and others negative. Expect myeloid cells scattered in the stroma or clustered at the edges of tumour nests, partly CD14+.
observed: A: strength differs a lot by core (some strongly yellow, some near-empty), not with nuclear density. B: patchy rings in some cell areas only. C: sparse, a few bright blobs. D: a mesh of rings round dark nuclei. E: partial white overlap with CD14, plus CD14-negative green.
why: Patchy ring staining in some cores and cell areas, not others, fits real PDL1, but contrast is low against grainy background and CD14 overlap is only partial.
notes: PDL1 shows rings round cells in some cores and in patches within B, plausibly tumour or myeloid. It is grainy, the bright blobs in C look like debris, and some PDL1 sits outside CD14 cells. A real but low-contrast stain.
